question: Why is it dangerous to rate-limit by the left-most X-Forwarded-For address?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki X-Forwarded-For ka left-most entry CLIENT khud likh sakta hai. Har hop -- client bhi -- is header mein likhta ya append karta hai. Agar hum left-most entry ko client ka IP maan lein, toh attacker har request ke saath ek naya fake address bhej dega (`X-Forwarded-For: 10.9.9.0`, `10.9.9.1`, ...) aur har baar usko ek fresh limit milegi. Matlab limit poori tarah bypass ho gayi -- login brute force ke liye sabse aasaan raasta.

Isliye ratelimit-kit mein default `trustedProxies: 0` hai: header ko poora IGNORE karo aur socket ka `remoteAddress` hi client hai. Socket address TCP connection se aata hai, usko client HTTP header se forge nahi kar sakta.

Yeh sirf theory nahi hai, test hai: `express.test.ts` mein capacity 2 ka limiter, aur 5 requests jinke X-Forwarded-For alag alag forged addresses hain (`10.9.9.0` se `10.9.9.4`). Result exactly `[200, 200, 429, 429, 429]` -- 2 allowed, 3 denied. Fake header se koi fresh limit nahi mili.

Aur mutation H1 ('client IP from the LEFT-most X-Forwarded-For') 4 tests fail karta hai, toh agar koi galti se yeh logic badal de, suite pakad legi.
why_needed: Rate limiter ka poora kaam 'yeh kaun hai' par tika hai. Agar identity client ke haath mein hai, toh limiter sirf imaandaar clients ko rokta hai -- attacker ko nahi.
real_world_analogy: Jaise building ke gate par visitor khud register mein apna naam likhe aur guard bina ID dekhe maan le. Ek hi aadmi har baar naya naam likh ke andar aa jayega. Guard ko sirf apni aankhon se dekhi cheez (socket address) par bharosa karna chahiye.
how_it_works: `clientIp(req, trustedProxies)` pehle check karta hai: agar `trustedProxies === 0` toh seedha `req.socket?.remoteAddress` return. Header padha hi nahi jaata. Phir `keyByIp()` us address ko `ipKey()` se `ip:1.2.3.4` jaisi key bana deta hai, aur RateLimiter us par prefix lagata hai.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts` mein `clientIp` ka comment hi poori kahani bata deta hai: 'X-Forwarded-For is written by EVERY hop, including the client itself'. Express middleware aur Nest guard dono ka default key `keyByIp()` hai, jo `trustedProxies ?? 0` use karta hai -- yaani secure default. `test/ip.test.ts` ka pehla test: `clientIp(req("10.0.0.5", "1.2.3.4"))` -> `10.0.0.5`.
advantages: Secure default: bina config ke koi bypass nahi
Socket address forge nahi ho sakta (TCP handshake chahiye)
Test aur mutation H1 dono isko guard karte hain
disadvantages: Proxy ke peeche default par sab clients ek hi IP (proxy ka) dikhenge -- sab ek limit share karenge, isliye proxy ke peeche trustedProxies set karna zaroori hai
common_mistakes: `req.headers['x-forwarded-for'].split(',')[0]` ko client IP maan lena
Express mein `trust proxy = true` laga dena (sab hops trusted) bina soche
Sirf load test se verify karna, forged-header test na likhna
follow_up_questions: Proxy ke peeche default 0 rakhoge toh kya hoga?
X-Real-IP header ke saath bhi yahi problem hai kya?
Socket address ko bhi spoof kiya ja sakta hai kya?

question: How does trustedProxies: n pick the client address, and why read from the right?
answer_hinglish:
Har proxy jo request forward karta hai, woh jo address usne DEKHA (apne socket par) usko X-Forwarded-For ke RIGHT end par append karta hai. Toh right side ki entries hamare apne proxies ne likhi hain -- woh trustworthy hain. Left side ki entries client ke control mein hain. Isliye `trustedProxies: n` ka matlab hai: 'mere n proxies aage baithe hain, toh right se n-th entry client hai.'

Example: client ne khud `6.6.6.6` bheja, hamare nginx ne asli address `203.0.113.9` append kiya. Header: `6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.9`. `trustedProxies: 1` -> `203.0.113.9`. Client ka fake `6.6.6.6` ignore ho gaya.

Implementation mein ek chhota sa trick hai: `clientIp` socket address ko bhi chain ke end mein jod deta hai (`[...hops, socketAddr]`) aur `chain[chain.length - 1 - trustedProxies]` leta hai. Socket address hamare last proxy ka hai, toh 1 trusted proxy par right-most header entry milti hai, 2 par doosri right se. Agar header mein expected se kam entries hain, `Math.max(0, ...)` left-most available leta hai -- yeh Express ke `trust proxy = n` jaisa hai.

Number galat hua toh dono taraf nuksaan: zyada rakha toh client-controlled entry trust ho jayegi (bypass); kam rakha toh sab users proxy ka IP share karenge (sab ek limit mein). Mutation H2 (count off by one) 5 tests fail karta hai.
why_needed: Production mein app hamesha nginx / load balancer ke peeche hota hai. Wahan socket address hamesha proxy ka hota hai, toh asli client header se hi nikalna padta hai -- par sirf trusted part se.
real_world_analogy: Courier parcel jab teen hubs se guzarta hai, har hub apni stamp neeche jodta hai. Sender upar kuch bhi likh sakta hai. Asli origin jaanne ke liye aap neeche se apne hubs ki stamps gin ke unke upar wali entry padhte ho -- upar likhi kahani nahi.
how_it_works: Header ko `,` par split, trim, khaali entries hatao. Repeated headers (array) pehle `,` se join hote hain, order maintained. Phir socket address append, aur right se `trustedProxies` steps peeche jao. `trustedProxies` negative ya fractional ho toh `RangeError`.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts::clientIp`. Tests `test/ip.test.ts` mein: 1 proxy (`6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.9` -> `203.0.113.9`), 2 proxies (`6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.9, 10.0.0.2` -> `203.0.113.9`), repeated headers, kam entries (`trustedProxies: 5` par `203.0.113.9`), invalid counts. Express test 'behind one trusted proxy': `6.6.6.6, <ip>` bhejke `[200, 200, 429]` -- clients proxy-appended address se alag pehchane gaye.

Ek number se config, Express ke trust proxy jaisa semantic
Multiple proxy layers (CDN + LB) support
disadvantages: Number deployment topology se match karna padta hai; topology badli toh config bhi
Kam entries par left-most fallback: agar koi proxy header append nahi karta toh galat entry mil sakti hai
common_mistakes: `trustedProxies` ko proxies ki jagah 'hops' samajh ke ek zyada rakh dena
CDN add kiya par count update nahi kiya
Proxy ko header REPLACE ki jagah client ka header pass-through karne dena bina append ke

Agar proxy client ka X-Forwarded-For overwrite kare toh?

question: Why does ratelimit-kit key IPv6 clients per /64 and normalise IPv4-mapped addresses?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag problems, ek hi goal: ek asli client = ek key.

Pehla, IPv6 /64. IPv6 mein ek subscriber (ghar ka router, ek VPS) ko usually poora /64 milta hai -- 2^64 addresses. Agar hum full address par limit karein, toh attacker har request ke liye naya address utha sakta hai aur har baar fresh limit. IPv4 mein address scarce hai isliye yeh nahi hota; IPv6 mein addresses free hain. Isliye `ipKey` pehle 4 hextets (64 bits) leta hai: `2001:db8:1:2::99` -> `ip6:2001:db8:1:2::/64`. Test 'every address in one /64 is ONE client' teen alag addresses ko ek key mein aur `aa:bc` wale ko alag key mein dikhata hai. Mutation H4 (full address keying) 7 tests fail karta hai.

Doosra, IPv4-mapped IPv6. Dual-stack Node server par IPv4 client ka socket address `::ffff:1.2.3.4` dikh sakta hai. Agar normalise na karein toh wahi client do keys (`ip:1.2.3.4` aur ek ip6 key) ke beech limit split kar sakta hai. Isliye `::ffff:` prefix (case-insensitive) hata ke `ip:1.2.3.4` banta hai. Mutation H3: 3 failures.

Zone id (`fe80::1%eth0`) bhi strip hota hai. Aur jo IP hi nahi hai, uske liye `undefined` -- matlab yeh limiter us request par apply hi nahi hota.

Trade-off: /64 mein ek se zyada users ho sakte hain (kuch ISPs ek /64 share karate hain) -- unhe ek limit share karni padegi. Strictness vs fairness ka conscious choice hai.
why_needed: IP-based limiting tabhi kaam karta hai jab attacker cheaply naye IPs na bana sake. IPv6 mein yeh assumption full-address level par toot jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel mein limit per ROOM lagao, per guest-naam nahi -- warna ek hi room ka aadmi har baar naya naam bata ke naya coupon le lega. /64 hi woh 'room' hai.
how_it_works: `ipKey`: trim, `::ffff:` + valid IPv4 ho toh slice, `%` ke baad sab hatao, `isIP()` se version. v4 -> `ip:<addr>`. v6 -> `expandIpv6()` jo `::` ko zeros mein expand karta hai, embedded IPv4 tail ko do hextets banata hai, leading zeros hatata hai; phir pehle 4 groups + `::/64`.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts::ipKey` aur helper `expandIpv6`. `test/ip.test.ts` ke cases: `2001:0db8:0001:0002:ffff::1` -> `ip6:2001:db8:1:2::/64` (leading zeros), `2001:db8::1` -> `ip6:2001:db8:0:0::/64`, `::1` -> `ip6:0:0:0:0::/64`, `fe80::1%eth0` -> `ip6:fe80:0:0:0::/64`, `not-an-ip` / `999.1.1.1` -> undefined. README ke mutation table mein H5 (zone id not stripped) equivalent hai: zone sirf last group mein hota hai aur /64 key pehle chaar rakhti hai, toh key kabhi nahi badalti.
advantages: Address rotation se bypass band
Dual-stack par ek client = ek key
Canonical form: same /64 ke alag spellings ek key
disadvantages: Shared /64 (kuch mobile / ISP setups) mein innocent users ek limit share karte hain
Non-IP address par limiter apply hi nahi hota -- silently unlimited (README isko document karta hai)
common_mistakes: IPv6 string ko as-is key bana dena (leading zeros / :: ke kaaran ek address ki kai spellings)
Sirf /128 par limit
`::ffff:` ko case-sensitive match karna (test dono cases check karta hai)
follow_up_questions: Kya /48 par bhi ek limit lagani chahiye?
IPv4 CGNAT ke peeche hazaron users ek IP share karein toh?
ipKey undefined return kare toh request ka kya hota hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: /64 strict hai par fair nahi -- ek shared /64 mein sab ek limit mein. Full address fair hai par trivially bypassable. Security limiter ke liye bypass zyada bura hai, isliye /64 chuna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar attacker ke paas /48 hai (65536 alag /64), toh woh phir bhi bahut saare keys bana sakta hai -- /64 grouping usse nahi rokti. Non-IP socket address (unix socket) par limiter skip ho jaata hai.
advanced.alternatives: Hierarchical limits: per /64 aur ek dheela per /48 limit stack karna (do `rateLimit` middlewares). Ya IP ki jagah account / API key par limit jahan possible ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada distinct IPv6 clients = zyada keys. Redis mein har key TTL se khatam hoti hai; MemoryStore `maxKeys` se bounded. Key count /64 grouping se ghat-ta hai, badhta nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: /48 level ka secondary limit (implement nahi hai, do limiters stack karke ho sakta hai), aur metrics ki kitni requests `ipKey` undefined ki wajah se unlimited gayi -- yeh bhi abhi nahi hai.

question: Rate-limit keys often come from user input. What does ratelimit-kit do to keep that safe?
answer_hinglish:
Key aksar client se aati hai -- IP, email, user id, header. Isse teen risks hain: bahut lambi key (memory / Redis bloat), collision (do alag limits ek state share kar lein), aur bahut saari distinct keys (memory attack). ratelimit-kit teeno ko alag jagah handle karta hai.

1. Length cap: `RateLimiter.consume` store ko touch karne SE PEHLE check karta hai -- key non-empty string ho aur 512 characters se zyada na ho (`MAX_KEY_LENGTH = 512`). 513 par `RateLimitError`. Test: 513 chars reject, exactly 512 pass. Mutation Q3 (off by one) 1 test fail karta hai.

2. Prefix: har limiter apna `prefix` lagata hai (default `rl:`), jaise `rl:login:`. Toh `ip:1.2.3.4` login limit mein `rl:login:ip:1.2.3.4` aur API limit mein `rl:api:ip:1.2.3.4` -- kabhi same state nahi. Key functions bhi type prefix lagate hain: `ip:`, `ip6:`, `email:`. Mutation Q1 (prefix not applied) 5 tests fail.

3. Distinct keys: MemoryStore `maxKeys` (default 100 000) par LRU eviction karta hai -- 100 000 keys with `maxKeys: 1000` -> exactly 1000. Redis mein har key PEXPIRE ke saath likhi jaati hai.

Ek aur cheez: README ka login key function (`byEmail`) email ko `trim().toLowerCase()` karta hai, taaki `Alice@x.com` aur `alice@x.com` alag limits na paayein -- aur email string na ho toh `undefined` return karta hai (yeh limiter skip, per-IP wala phir bhi lagta hai), `email:undefined` nahi, jo har bina-email request ko EK shared bucket mein daal deta. Validation `RateLimitError` deti hai -- jo ek bug hai, isliye yeh kabhi fail-open nahi hota.
why_needed: Jo cheez attacker control karta hai, woh hamare datastore ki key ban rahi hai. Bina bounds ke yeh ek free memory-allocation API ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Locker room mein har locker par naam ka label: label ki max length fixed hai, har department ka apna color (prefix), aur lockers ki total ginti limited hai -- naye ke liye sabse purana khaali hota hai.
how_it_works: Validation order: key type/empty -> length -> cost integer >= 1 -> cost <= limit. Phir `this.prefix + key` store ko jaata hai. Store kabhi unvalidated key nahi dekhta (test 'rejects ... before touching the store' recording store se verify karta hai ki `keys` khaali raha).
in_this_project: `src/limiter.ts::RateLimiter` mein `MAX_KEY_LENGTH` aur prefix; `test/limiter.test.ts` mein prefixes test (`rl:ip:1.2.3.4` vs `rl:login:ip:1.2.3.4`), validation cases, aur 100 000 keys wala MemoryStore test. README ka Express example: `const byEmail = (req) => (typeof req.body?.email === "string" ? `email:${req.body.email.trim().toLowerCase()}` : undefined);` with the comment 'NOT `email:${undefined}`: that would put every request without an email into ONE shared bucket'.
advantages: Store tak sirf validated, namespaced keys pahunchti hain
Limits ke beech accidental state sharing nahi
Memory bounded (MemoryStore) / time-bounded (Redis TTL)
disadvantages: 512 ki cap characters par hai, bytes par nahi -- multi-byte chars Redis mein zyada bytes
Ek over-long key request ko error handler bhejti hai (500 jaisa), 429 nahi -- client ko lagega server bug
common_mistakes: Raw email bina normalise kiye key banana
Har limiter ka same prefix rakhna
Key mein poora request body ya token daal dena
`email:${undefined}` -- missing field par ek shared 'email:undefined' bucket ban jaana (README ka byEmail isi liye undefined return karta hai)
follow_up_questions: Lambi key ko hash karke chhota kyun nahi kiya?
Email key aur IP key dono kyun chahiye login par?
Key mein PII (email) Redis mein store karna theek hai kya?

question: How should a login or OTP limit be configured, and why must it fail closed?
answer_hinglish:
Login / OTP / password reset limits SECURITY ke liye hain: inka kaam guessing ko slow karna hai. Isliye do cheezein: per-IP AUR per-account dono limits, aur Redis down ho toh fail CLOSED.

Stacking: sirf per-IP limit botnet nahi rokta (har bot ka alag IP), sirf per-account limit ek IP se hazaron accounts try karna nahi rokta. README ka Nest example dono decorators stack karta hai: `@RateLimit(loginIpLimit)` aur `@RateLimit(loginUserLimit, { key: byEmail })` -- byEmail email na ho toh undefined deta hai (per-account limit skip, per-IP phir bhi), taaki bina-email requests ek shared `email:undefined` bucket mein na jaayein. Stacked limiters sab apply hote hain, pehla denial jeetta hai. README ka example number: sliding window `limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000` -- 5 tries per 15 minutes. Sliding window isliye kyunki fixed window ke edge par double burst milta hai.

Fail closed: agar Redis down hai aur limiter 'allow' kare, toh attacker ko UNLIMITED guesses mil gaye -- bilkul tab jab hum kamzor hain. Isliye `onStoreError: "deny"`: response 503, `Retry-After: 5`, body `{"error":"rate_limit_unavailable",...}`, route nahi chalta. 503 isliye, 429 nahi: galti server ki hai, client ne limit cross nahi ki. Mutations O2 (429 instead of 503) aur O3 (no Retry-After) dono pakde gaye.

Ek nuance: agar aap is limit ke store par `FailoverStore` + MemoryStore fallback lagao, toh 'deny' kabhi trigger nahi hoga -- fallback answer dega (per instance, N x limit). Login ke liye decide karo: degraded limit chalega ya strict deny chahiye.
why_needed: Brute force aur OTP guessing tabhi practical hote hain jab attempts unlimited hon. 6-digit OTP sirf 10^6 combinations hai -- limit hi asli security hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank locker: teen galat code ke baad locker band. Agar locker ka counter kharab ho jaye, toh bank locker khula nahi chhodta -- 'abhi service nahi, baad mein aaiye' bolta hai.
how_it_works: Adapter catch block: `RateLimitError` ya mode `error` -> rethrow; `allow` -> `next()`; warna 503 + `retry-after` + JSON body. Nest mein `res.setHeader('retry-after')` phir `HttpException(STORE_UNAVAILABLE_BODY, 503)`.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/express.ts::rateLimit` aur `src/adapters/nestjs.ts::RateLimitGuard` mein `onStoreError`. Constants `src/adapters/http.ts` mein: `STORE_UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AFTER_S = 5`, `STORE_UNAVAILABLE_BODY`. `test/failover.test.ts` mein real ioredis client closed port (`127.0.0.1:1`) par: 'deny' -> `[503, "5", "rate_limit_unavailable"]`. Nest test: deny -> 503 + Retry-After.
advantages: Attacker outage ka fayda nahi utha sakta
503 + Retry-After clients aur monitoring ko sahi signal deta hai
Per-route choice: API fail-open, login fail-closed
disadvantages: Redis outage mein legit users bhi login nahi kar paate -- availability ki keemat
Per-account limit se attacker kisi victim ko lock out kar sakta hai (account lockout DoS)
common_mistakes: Login par global default 'allow' laga dena
Sirf per-IP limit
Fail-closed par 429 bhejna -- client sochega usne kuch galat kiya
Login store par MemoryStore fallback lagake sochna ki ab bhi strict hai
follow_up_questions: Per-account limit se lockout DoS kaise rokoge?
OTP ke liye per-phone limit aur per-IP dono kyun?
503 ka Retry-After 5 hi kyun, configurable kyun nahi?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fail closed = security first, availability second. Capacity limits ke liye ulta. ratelimit-kit yeh choice per limit deta hai, global nahi -- yahi design ka point hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis down + deny = login band. Agar breaker open hai toh 10 s (`openMs` jaisa config) tak sab 503. Per-account lockout se attacker victim ko lock kar sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Degraded strictness: MemoryStore fallback (N x limit) -- outage mein bhi login chalta hai par limit dheeli. Ya CAPTCHA step after N failures (implement nahi). Ya exponential backoff per account.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x instances par degraded fallback N x limit tak dheela ho jaata hai -- 10 instances = 50 tries per 15 min. Isliye security limits par fallback sochke lagao.
advanced.production_improvements: Failed attempts ko hi count karna (success par reset) -- abhi limiter har attempt count karta hai, success/failure ka fark nahi. Alerting on 503 rate. Retry-After configurable karna (abhi constant 5).

question: Why is a RateLimitError never failed open, and are there gaps in that guarantee?
answer_hinglish:
Fail open ka matlab hai: 'store se jawab nahi mila, toh request jaane do.' Yeh capacity limits ke liye theek hai jab problem INFRA ki ho. Lekin agar error ek BUG hai -- galat key, cost limit se zyada, fractional cost -- toh fail-open ka matlab hoga ki ek code bug chupchaap limiter ko band kar de aur koi notice bhi na kare. Isliye adapters mein pehla check hai: `if (error instanceof RateLimitError || onStoreError === "error") throw error;`. Bug hamesha error handler tak jaata hai, 'allow' ke saath bhi.

Test: route par `onStoreError: "allow"` aur `cost: () => 99` (capacity 2). Store dead hai, phir bhi response 'error handler' -- kyunki RateLimiter store ko call karne se pehle hi `RateLimitError` deta hai. Express aur Nest dono ke liye test hai, mutations O1 aur O7 pakde gaye.

Ek gap jo THA aur fix hua: pehle stage-3 version mein user ka `cost()` function try block ke andar call hota tha, toh agar woh TypeError throw kare, 'allow' par request fail OPEN ho jaati. Interview bank likhte waqt review mein pakda gaya; ab dono adapters cost ko (key ki tarah) try ke BAHAR compute karte hain, aur throwing cost function error handler tak jaata hai -- har adapter ke liye ek test (`test/failover.test.ts` 'a throwing cost function (a bug) is never failed open either', `test/nestjs.test.ts` `/down/bug2` -> 500).

Jo gaps abhi bhi hain, code padh ke:
1. Guarantee sirf `RateLimitError` CLASS ke liye hai (aur key / cost functions ke liye, jo store call ke bahar chalte hain). `limiter.consume` ka baaki har error 'store error' maana jaata hai -- README ka 'Scope of onStoreError': sirf StoreUnavailableError nahi, RedisStore ka 'unexpected reply from the rate-limit script' ya 'script SHA mismatch' bhi (yeh bhi bugs ho sakte hain) fail open / closed hote hain.
2. `instanceof` check: agar app mein package ki do copies load ho jaayein, class identity alag hogi.
3. Fail-open requests kahin count nahi hoti -- README kehta hai uske around logging khud lagao.

Production mein main StoreUnavailableError ko explicit check karta (allow-list).
why_needed: Fail-open ek dangerous switch hai: woh errors ko silence karta hai. Silence sirf unhi errors ke liye honi chahiye jinhe hum samajhte hain (infra down), bugs ke liye nahi.
real_world_analogy: Building ka fire door: bijli jaaye toh door khul jaata hai (fail open, safety ke liye). Lekin agar lock ka software hi galat code accept kar raha ho, toh aap door hamesha khula nahi chhodte -- aap usko repair ticket banate ho.
how_it_works: `RateLimiter.consume` validation fail par `RateLimitError` deta hai. Algorithm constructors (`tokenBucket`, `slidingWindow`) bhi bad options par RateLimitError dete hain. Adapter catch mein class check pehle, phir mode. `StoreUnavailableError` FailoverStore se aata hai, lekin adapter usko explicitly check nahi karta -- woh 'baaki sab' bucket mein hai.
in_this_project: `src/types.ts` ka comment: 'A programming / input error ... Never a reason to fail open'. `src/adapters/express.ts` aur `src/adapters/nestjs.ts` ka catch block. Tests: `test/failover.test.ts` ('a bug (cost above the limit) is never failed open') aur `test/nestjs.test.ts` ka `/down/bug` route -> 500; throwing cost function ke liye `test/failover.test.ts` ('a throwing cost function (a bug) is never failed open either') aur Nest ka `/down/bug2` -> 500. Fix code mein: `const cost = options.cost?.(req) ?? 1;` try ke bahar, comment 'a throwing cost function is a bug in the app, never a store error to fail open on'. README 'When Redis is down' mein found-and-fixed aur 'Scope of onStoreError' likha hai.

Explicit error taxonomy: RateLimitError vs StoreUnavailableError
Dono frameworks mein same rule, tested
disadvantages: Allow-list nahi, deny-list hai: unknown errors fail-open ho jaate hain
Pehle version mein throwing cost function 'allow' par silently bypass karta tha (ab fixed; mutation run us fix se pehle ka hai)
common_mistakes: `catch (e) { next() }` -- har error par fail open
Validation ko store ke baad karna
Fail-open errors ko log na karna

Fail-open hone wali requests ko kaise count / alert karoge?
Duplicate package copies mein instanceof kyun fail hota hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Deny-list (sirf RateLimitError rethrow) simple hai aur raw Redis errors (FailoverStore ke bina) ko bhi handle karta hai -- dead-port tests mein RedisStore seedha use hota hai aur raw ioredis error 'allow'/'deny' trigger karta hai. Allow-list zyada safe hoti par tab har user ko FailoverStore lagana padta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Fix se pehle: ek cost function jo kisi naye request shape par TypeError de, 'allow' route par limiter ko poori tarah band kar deta bina 500 ke -- ab woh 500 deta hai. Abhi bhi: ek corrupted script (SHA mismatch) ya unexpected reply fail-open hoga.
advanced.alternatives: `error instanceof StoreUnavailableError || isConnectionError(error)` par hi allow; `cost()` aur `key()` dono try ke bahar (ab yahi hai); ya error code (`error.name`) based check instead of instanceof.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada routes aur zyada custom key/cost functions = zyada chances ki koi throw kare -- yeh ab error handler tak jaate hain. Scale par baaki gap (store-side bugs fail-open) real hai.

question: What do the 429 and 503 responses reveal to the client, and is sending RateLimit headers a risk?
answer_hinglish:
429 body fixed hai: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Too many requests. Try again later."}`. 503 (fail closed) body bhi fixed: `{"error":"rate_limit_unavailable","message":"Please try again shortly."}`. Dono `src/adapters/http.ts` mein constants hain -- Redis ka error text, key, prefix, ya stack trace kabhi body mein nahi jaata. Client ko ek stable machine-readable `error` code milta hai, bas.

Headers zyada batate hain: `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds, rounded up), aur denial par `Retry-After` (kam se kam 1). Kya yeh risk hai? Ek attacker inse exactly jaan leta hai ki limit kitni hai aur kab reset hogi -- toh woh limit ke just neeche rehke 'low and slow' attack kar sakta hai. Lekin limit chhupana security nahi hai: attacker 429 aane tak probe karke bhi yeh seekh lega. Imaandaar clients ke liye headers bahut useful hain -- woh backoff kar sakte hain.

Isliye default `headers: true`, par `headers: false` option hai: allowed responses par RateLimit-* nahi jaate. 429 par headers hamesha jaate hain (E1 mutation -- 429 without headers -- pakda gaya), kyunki denied client ko Retry-After chahiye. Login jaise sensitive route par main `headers: false` rakhta.

Ek aur detail: 'allow' (fail-open) path par headers nahi jaate (test: `ratelimit-limit` null) -- jab koi decision hi nahi hai toh fake numbers nahi bhejte.
why_needed: Error responses information disclosure ka common source hain, aur rate limit headers ek deliberate disclosure hain -- dono ko sochke design karna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Traffic police ka board 'Speed limit 60' -- limit batana koi nahi chhupata. Lekin challan par aap camera ka model number aur server ka IP nahi likhte.
how_it_works: `rateLimitHeaders(d)` decision se headers banata hai; `setHeaders` sirf tab jab `res.headersSent` false ho. Adapter: `if (sendHeaders || !decision.allowed) setHeaders(res, decision)`. Body `res.end(JSON.stringify(TOO_MANY_REQUESTS_BODY))` (Express) ya `HttpException(TOO_MANY_REQUESTS_BODY, 429)` (Nest).
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts` mein `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS_BODY`, `STORE_UNAVAILABLE_BODY`, `rateLimitHeaders`. `test/express.test.ts`: denied body exactly `{ error: "rate_limited", message: "Too many requests. Try again later." }`; 'headers: false' test -> allowed par null, 429 par `ratelimit-limit` '1' aur Retry-After present. `test/ip.test.ts`: Retry-After rounding (2001 ms -> '3', 0 ms -> '1').

Stable `error` codes client logic ke liye
Headers optional on success, guaranteed on 429
disadvantages: Headers se attacker limit ko exactly calibrate kar sakta hai
Body English mein hardcoded, customize karne ka option nahi
common_mistakes: 429 body mein key ya prefix daal dena ('rl:login:email:x limited')
Retry-After 0 bhejna -- client turant retry karega (H6 mutation)
503 aur 429 ko same body dena

question: How are Redis keys named in ratelimit-kit, and why does every limiter get its own prefix?
answer_hinglish:
Redis key = limiter ka `prefix` + key function ki key. Example: login limiter `prefix: "rl:login:"`, key function `email:alice@x.com` -> Redis key `rl:login:email:alice@x.com`. IP wala: `rl:api:ip:203.0.113.9` ya `rl:api:ip6:2001:db8:1:2::/64`. Default prefix `rl:` hai.

Prefix kyun? Ek hi user (ya IP) par aksar kai limits lagti hain -- API limit, login limit, OTP limit. Agar sab same key use karein toh ek limit ke requests doosri ka budget kha jaayenge -- 3 API calls ke baad user login bhi nahi kar payega, ya ulta. Isliye rule: ek limit = ek prefix. Test `limiter.test.ts` dikhata hai ki same `ip:1.2.3.4` do limiters mein `rl:ip:1.2.3.4` aur `rl:login:ip:1.2.3.4` ban jaata hai. Mutation Q1 (prefix not applied) 5 tests tod deta hai.

Colon (`:`) Redis ka convention hai namespaces ke liye -- tools (RedisInsight, `SCAN MATCH rl:login:*`) isse group karte hain. Tests bhi isi ka fayda uthate hain: har run apna `rltest:<pid>:` prefix use karta hai aur end mein `KEYS rltest:<pid>:*` se cleanup karta hai.

Sliding window ek level aur jodta hai: Lua script base key ke peeche `:<window start>` lagata hai, toh actual Redis keys `rl:login:email:alice@x.com:1700000000000` jaisi hoti hain.
why_needed: Redis mein schema nahi hota -- key naming hi aapka schema hai. Galat naming = data collision ya cleanup impossible.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi almari mein alag files ke liye alag colored folders: 'login' folder aur 'api' folder. Same customer ka naam dono mein ho sakta hai, par papers mix nahi hote.
how_it_works: `RateLimiter` constructor `this.prefix = options.prefix ?? "rl:"`, `consume` mein `this.prefix + key` store ko pass. RedisStore woh string `KEYS[1]` ke roop mein EVALSHA ko deta hai. Lua token bucket seedha `KEYS[1]` par HASH; sliding window `KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start`.
in_this_project: `src/limiter.ts` (prefix, comment: 'one prefix per limit, so a login limit and an API limit for the same user never share state'), `src/adapters/http.ts` (key types `ip:` / `ip6:`), `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` (window suffix), `test/redis.test.ts` (`PREFIX = `rltest:${process.pid}:``).

-- real, src/lua/sliding_counter.lua
local cur_start = now - (now % window)
local prev_start = cur_start - window
local cur_key = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start
local prev_key = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. prev_start

SCAN / monitoring ke liye readable namespaces
Tests parallel aur safely cleanup kar sakte hain

Long prefixes har key ke bytes badhate hain

Production mein `KEYS rl:*` chalana (blocking) -- SCAN use karo
Prefix ke end mein `:` bhool jaana (`rl:loginip:...`)

question: What exactly does the sliding window counter store in Redis, and how long does it live?
answer_hinglish:
Har client ke liye do STRING counters, ek per window: `<key>:<window start ms>`. Current window ka counter aur previous window ka counter. Bas -- O(1) memory per client, chahe limit 5 ho ya 5000. Sliding LOG har request ka timestamp rakhta (memory per request); yeh design wahi problem avoid karta hai.

Lua script kya karta hai: `cur_start = now - (now % window)`, phir `GET` current aur previous key (missing = 0). Estimate = `cur + prev * weight`, jahan weight = previous window ka kitna hissa abhi bhi sliding window ke andar hai. Agar `estimated + cost > limit` -> denied aur script turant RETURN karta hai -- kuch likhta hi nahi. Denied requests count nahi hoti (mutation U2 Lua mein yeh todta hai, real Redis test pakadta hai). Allowed par `INCRBY cur_key cost` aur `PEXPIRE cur_key window * 2`.

TTL 2 windows kyun? Current window ka counter agle window mein 'previous' ban ke kaam aata hai. Do windows ke baad woh kabhi read nahi hoga, toh Redis usko khud delete kar deta hai. Do windows peeche wala counter estimate mein count bhi nahi hota (test 'a window two or more back no longer counts', mutation S4).

Note: key window START se bani hai, toh har naye window mein ek nayi key banti hai -- ek active client ke liye max 2 live keys. Ek detail: har allowed request PEXPIRE refresh karta hai, toh TTL last write se 2 windows hai. Agar window ka sirf pehla ms mein ek write hua, key agle window ke end tak zinda rehti hai -- exactly utni der jitni 'previous' ke roop mein chahiye.
why_needed: Datastore design ka sawaal: per client kitna data, kab tak, aur kaun delete karega. TTL ke bina har IP jo kabhi aaya woh hamesha Redis mein rehta.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan ka register jismein sirf do pages: is ghante ka count aur pichhle ghante ka. Teesre ghante ka page phaad ke phenk do -- uski zaroorat kabhi nahi padegi.
how_it_works: Key: `KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start`. Reads: do GET. Write: sirf allowed par INCRBY + PEXPIRE(window*2). Reply: `{allowed, remaining, retry, reset}` jahan reset = `window - elapsed`.
in_this_project: `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` (project 1 se unchanged copy). TypeScript mirror `src/algorithms.ts::slidingWindow` mein state `{start, count, prevCount}` hai jo 'what Redis would find under the keys for the current and the previous window' ko model karta hai. Real Redis atomicity test: 200 concurrent, limit 40 -> exactly 40.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/sliding_counter.lua (tail)
if estimated + cost > limit then
  -- ... retry calculation ...
  return {0, math.max(math.floor(limit - estimated), 0), math.max(retry, 1), window - elapsed}
end

cur = redis.call('INCRBY', cur_key, cost)
-- Keep it for 2 windows: it is needed as "previous" during the next window.
redis.call('PEXPIRE', cur_key, window * 2)
return {1, math.max(math.floor(limit - (cur + prev * weight)), 0), 0, window - elapsed}
advantages: O(1) memory per client
Redis khud cleanup karta hai (TTL)
Denied requests koi write nahi karte -- attack ke dauran Redis writes kam
disadvantages: Approximate: exact tabhi jab previous window ke requests evenly spread hon
Per client 2 keys, ek hash ki jagah -- Cluster mein undeclared keys ki problem
common_mistakes: TTL = 1 window rakhna (previous counter jaldi mar jaayega, limit dheeli)
Denied requests ko bhi INCR karna -- attacker khud ko hamesha blocked rakhega aur legit retry bhi
Window start ko app clock se calculate karna jab instances ke clocks drift karein

Window start ko key mein kyun, ek hash mein do fields kyun nahi?
Estimate kab galat hota hai?

question: How does the token bucket store its state in Redis, and why is the stored token count rounded?
answer_hinglish:
Ek HASH per client, do fields: `tokens` (fractional count) aur `ts` (last update ka ms timestamp). Lua script `HMGET key tokens ts` karta hai; agar `tokens` nil hai toh naya client -- full bucket (`capacity`) aur `ts = now`. Phir lazy refill: `tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * rate / 1000)`, koi timer nahi. Decision ke baad `HSET key tokens tostring(tokens) ts tostring(now)` aur `PEXPIRE key ceil(capacity*1000/rate) + 1000`.

TTL ka logic: bucket khaali se full hone mein `capacity / rate` seconds lagte hain. Utni der koi request na aaye toh bucket full hai -- aur full bucket bilkul 'koi state nahi' jaisa hai. Isliye key delete ho jaye toh koi fark nahi; +1 s margin hai. Test: capacity 2, rate 1 -> PTTL > 0 aur <= 3000. Mutation U3 (no expiry) real Redis test se pakda gaya.

Rounding kyun? Redis ka Lua `tostring()` number ko `%.14g` -- 14 significant digits -- mein convert karta hai. Toh Redis mein stored token count thoda rounded hai. TypeScript MemoryStore ko IDENTICAL decisions dene hain, isliye woh bhi stored value ko `luaToString(x) = Number(x.toPrecision(14))` se round karta hai. Lekin reply (`remaining`, `resetMs`) full-precision variable se aata hai -- pehle version ne dono round kiye aur parity test seed 1 step 91 par `resetMs` 1135 vs 1136 se fail hua. Mutation L1 (no rounding) bhi parity test fail karta hai.

Hash kyun, do keys kyun nahi? Dono fields hamesha saath padhe/likhe jaate hain -- ek key, ek TTL, ek slot.
why_needed: Token bucket ko continuous state chahiye (fractional tokens + time). Usko kaise serialize karo, yeh decide karta hai ki do implementations (Lua aur TS) agree karenge ya nahi.
real_world_analogy: Paani ki tanki jismein meter hai: aapko har second paani bharte dekhne ki zaroorat nahi -- last reading aur time note kar lo, agli baar formula se nikaal lo kitna bhara.
how_it_works: HMGET -> refill (clock backwards par `max(now - ts, 0)`) -> allow/deny -> HSET tostring -> PEXPIRE -> reply `{allowed, floor(tokens), retry, reset}`. Denied request bhi HSET karta hai (refilled value + new ts), par tokens nahi ghatata.
in_this_project: `src/lua/token_bucket.lua` aur TS mirror `src/algorithms.ts::tokenBucket` (`luaToString`). Parity: `test/redis.test.ts` 3 seeds x 200 steps, capacity 5, refill 3/s. TTL sirf Lua script set karta hai (PEXPIRE); MemoryStore mein koi expiry nahi -- wahan idle state waise bhi fresh state jaisi behave karti hai.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/token_bucket.lua (tail)
-- Store state with full precision (tostring keeps the fraction).
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tostring(tokens), 'ts', tostring(now))
-- After capacity/rate seconds the bucket is full again, so state can be dropped.
redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], math.ceil(capacity * 1000 / rate) + 1000)

local reset = math.ceil((capacity - tokens) * 1000 / rate)
return {allowed, math.floor(tokens), retry, reset}
advantages: Ek key per client, ek TTL
Lazy refill: koi background job nahi
Full bucket ke baad state automatically gayab
disadvantages: Lua ka purana comment 'full precision' kehta hai par tostring 14 significant digits par round karta hai (file ke top par ab iska note hai) -- isi wajah se TS ko mirror karna pada
Denied request bhi ek HSET write karta hai
common_mistakes: TS memory store ko full precision rakhna -- Redis se decisions mismatch
Reply bhi rounded value se banana (1 ms ka bug)
TTL fixed rakhna (e.g. 1 hour) -- rate chhota ho toh state jaldi mar jaayegi aur bucket galat refill

Clock backwards jaaye toh kya hota hai?
Hash ki jagah ek string mein 'tokens:ts' rakhte toh?

question: How would you estimate Redis memory for rate-limit keys, and what bounds it?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baat: is project mein Redis memory measure NAHI ki gayi -- README mein koi bytes-per-key number nahi hai. Toh main method batata hoon, measured number nahi.

Formula: live keys x bytes per key. Live keys kitni hain, yeh TTL decide karta hai, total users nahi:
- Token bucket: ek HASH per client, jo `capacity/rate + 1 s` silence ke baad expire hoti hai. Toh live keys = pichhle (capacity/rate + 1) seconds mein active distinct clients. Capacity 20, refill 5/s (README ka API example) -> sirf ~5 s window!
- Sliding window: per active client 1-2 STRING keys, TTL `2 x window`. Login 15 min window -> 30 min tak keys rehti hain.

Bytes per key: key name (prefix + `ip:...` ya `email:...`, max 512 chars RateLimiter allow karta hai) + Redis per-key overhead (dict entry, expiry entry, object header) + value. Chhote hashes Redis listpack encoding mein compact rehte hain. Typically ek chhoti key ka total order of magnitude ~100 bytes hota hai -- yeh generic ballpark hai, measure karna chahiye: `MEMORY USAGE <key>` sample keys par aur `INFO memory`.

Example (illustrative): 1 lakh active IPs x 2 sliding keys x ~100 bytes = ~20 MB order. Kuch nahi. Asli khatra: attacker distinct keys banaye (IPv6 rotation, random emails). /64 grouping aur 512-char cap madad karte hain; Redis mein `maxmemory` + eviction policy set karna production ka kaam hai. MemoryStore side par `maxKeys` (default 100 000) hard bound hai.
why_needed: Rate limiter attack ke time sabse zyada load leta hai -- agar wahi time uska datastore OOM ho jaye toh limiter khud outage ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Parking lot ka size total customers se nahi, ek waqt par khadi gaadiyon (active within TTL) se decide hota hai.
how_it_works: TTL-driven working set: keys automatically expire. Short TTL = chhota working set. Distinct-key flood working set ko badhata hai -- uski defense key normalization (/64, lowercase) aur length cap hai.
in_this_project: TTLs `src/lua/token_bucket.lua` (PEXPIRE capacity/rate + 1 s) aur `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` (window * 2). Key length cap `src/limiter.ts` (512). MemoryStore bound `src/memory-store.ts` (maxKeys, LRU; 100 000 keys + maxKeys 1000 -> 1000, test). Redis memory ka koi measurement ya test repo mein nahi hai.

redis-cli MEMORY USAGE 'rl:login:email:alice@example.com:1700000000000'

MemoryStore ka hard cap
disadvantages: Redis side koi hard cap library mein nahi -- maxmemory ops ko set karna
Long keys (emails, 512 chars tak) bytes badhate hain

Token bucket ka TTL mathematically 'free' hai (full = no state), sliding ka bhi (2 windows ke baad counter use nahi hota) -- toh yahan memory aur correctness mein trade-off nahi, design hi tight hai.

advanced.alternatives: Approximate structures (count-min sketch) heavy hitters ke liye; ya per-key hashing se fixed-size key; ya rate-limit ke liye dedicated Redis instance.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x active clients = 10x keys linear. 100x par ek Redis ki memory aur CPU dono dekhne padenge -- Cluster (yahan tested nahi) ya sharding by prefix.

question: Should the Redis behind a rate limiter be persistent? What happens to limits on a restart?
answer_hinglish:
Agar Redis restart ho aur data persist nahi hua, toh saari rate-limit keys gayab -- matlab har client ko FRESH limit mil jaati hai. Token bucket full, sliding window zero. Yeh 'fail open for one window' jaisa hai.

Kitna bura hai, yeh limit par depend karta hai:
- API capacity limit (bursts of 20, 5/s): bucket waise bhi kuch seconds mein refill hota hai. Restart ka asar negligible. Persistence ki zaroorat nahi.
- Login 5 per 15 min: attacker ko restart par 5 extra tries. Agar attacker restarts trigger kar sake (ya Redis baar baar crash ho), toh har baar 5 extra. Phir bhi brute force ke liye yeh bahut kam hai.

Redis ke options: RDB snapshot (periodic, minutes ka data loss), AOF `everysec` (max ~1 s loss, har write disk par), ya kuch nahi. Rate-limit data short-lived hai aur write-heavy hai (har allowed request ek write) -- AOF ka write cost har request par lagta hai. Isliye mera recommendation: capacity limits ke liye persistence off; agar security limits same Redis par hain aur restart frequent hain, toh AOF everysec consider karo.

Is repo mein: infra Redis `--appendonly no --save ""` se chalta hai -- poori tarah non-persistent. Yeh dev/test ke liye hai; production persistence configure karna library ka kaam nahi, ops ka hai. Library ki taraf se restart ka doosra asar -- script cache khaali -> NOSCRIPT -- handle hota hai: RedisStore script load karke ek baar retry karta hai (test SCRIPT FLUSH ke saath).
why_needed: Datastore choose karte waqt poochna padta hai: is data ko khona kitna mehenga hai? Rate-limit state ke liye answer usually 'thoda', aur yahi Redis ko bina heavy persistence ke chalane deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Gym ka daily entry counter: agar register kho jaaye toh aaj sabko ek extra entry mil jayegi -- koi badi baat nahi. Bank ka ledger kho jaye toh disaster. Pehle ke liye fireproof safe nahi khareedte.
how_it_works: Restart -> keyspace khaali (no persistence) -> HMGET/GET nil -> 'new identity' path (full bucket / zero count). Script cache bhi khaali -> EVALSHA NOSCRIPT -> SCRIPT LOAD -> retry.
in_this_project: `infra/docker-compose.yml` ka Redis service: `command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "no", "--save", ""]`. `src/redis-store.ts` NOSCRIPT handling; `test/redis.test.ts` 'NOSCRIPT after SCRIPT FLUSH (e.g. a Redis restart)': flush ke baad bhi `{ allowed: true, remaining: 1 }` -- yaani state (keys) bachi, sirf script cache gaya. Keys ka loss is repo mein test nahi kiya gaya.

  image: redis:7-alpine
  command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "no", "--save", ""]
  ports: ["127.0.0.1:56379:6379"]

advanced.alternatives: AOF everysec; ya security counters ko durable DB mein (e.g. failed-login count Postgres mein) aur Redis sirf fast path ke liye; ya restart ke baad kuch der fail-closed.

question: Can rate-limit checks be sent to a Redis replica? What does ratelimit-kit do with READONLY?
answer_hinglish:
Nahi. Har rate-limit check ek WRITE hai -- token bucket har call par HSET + PEXPIRE karta hai, sliding window allowed par INCRBY + PEXPIRE. Ek 'read-decide-write' ko atomic hona chahiye, isliye woh primary par hi chalna chahiye. Replica writes refuse karta hai: `READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.`

Kab hota hai yeh practically? (1) Koi galti se client ko replica ka URL de de. (2) Failover ke baad purana connection ek aise node par hai jo ab replica ban gaya. (3) Read scaling ke liye 'replica reads' enable kiya aur script wahan chala gaya.

RedisStore ka behaviour: sirf `NOSCRIPT` par retry (script load karke ek baar). Baaki har error -- READONLY bhi -- seedha pass through, retry NAHI. Test: ek fake client jo hamesha READONLY throw karta hai -> `consume` READONLY ke saath reject, aur `calls` exactly 1. Mutation R2 ('every error retried as if NOSCRIPT') isi test se pakda gaya.

Retry kyun nahi? READONLY retry se theek nahi hota -- same node par same error milega, bas latency double. Uska fix connection-level hai: client ko naye primary par reconnect karna (Sentinel-aware client ya ioredis ka reconnect-on-error config). Library ko apna Redis client nahi chahiye -- 'bring your own client' -- isliye topology handling bhi client ki responsibility hai.

Error upar jaata hai: FailoverStore hai toh fallback / StoreUnavailableError, aur adapter ka `onStoreError` decide karta hai.
why_needed: Replica reads ek common scaling trick hai, par stateful counters ke liye galat hai. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap read vs write path samajhte ho.
real_world_analogy: Bank branch ke photocopy register se balance padh sakte ho, par usmein entry nahi kar sakte -- entry sirf main ledger mein.
how_it_works: `RedisStore.consume`: `try { evalsha } catch (error) { if (!message.includes("NOSCRIPT")) throw error; scriptLoad; evalsha }`. String match error message par hai.

question: Would ratelimit-kit work on Redis Cluster? What would you change?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: Redis Cluster par yeh TEST nahi hua, aur sliding window as-is fail ho sakta hai. README ise 'NOT implemented' list mein clearly likhta hai.

Kyun? Cluster mein har key ek hash slot mein jaati hai (CRC16 of key mod 16384), aur slots alag nodes par. Ek Lua script sirf us node ki keys chhoo sakta hai, aur Redis expect karta hai ki script ki saari keys `KEYS[]` mein declare hon taaki client sahi node par bheje.

- Token bucket: ek hi key, `KEYS[1]` -- declared. Cluster par theek rehna chahiye (par test nahi kiya).
- Sliding window: script `KEYS[1]` declare karta hai, par andar do NAYI keys banata hai -- `KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start` aur prev. Yeh undeclared hain aur unka hash slot base key se alag ho sakta hai. Doosre node par hon toh Redis non-local key access refuse karta hai.

Fix: hash tag. Cluster sirf `{...}` ke andar ka part hash karta hai. Agar key `rl:login:{email:alice@x.com}` ho, toh `rl:login:{email:alice@x.com}:1700000000000` bhi usi slot mein. README yahi suggest karta hai (`{user42}`) -- 'not done or tested here'. Behtar fix: script ko change karke window keys ko bhi KEYS mein pass karna, par Lua scripts project 1 se UNCHANGED reuse kiye gaye hain (unka testing history bachaane ke liye) -- toh woh ek conscious cost hai.

Doosri cheez: `RedisScriptClient` interface sirf `evalsha` aur `scriptLoad` hai. Cluster client ko scriptLoad har node par karna padta hai; NOSCRIPT-retry per node chalega, par yeh bhi verify nahi hua.
why_needed: Ek Redis ki memory/CPU limit aane par Cluster natural next step hai. Multi-key Lua scripts wahi jagah hain jahan Cluster migrations toot-ti hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek file ke do pages alag almariyon mein rakh do toh clerk ek hi trip mein dono nahi padh sakta. Hash tag = sab pages par same almari ka sticker.
how_it_works: Slot = CRC16(hashable part) % 16384. Hashable part = `{` aur pehle `}` ke beech ka text agar non-empty ho, warna poori key. Script execution ek node par; undeclared cross-slot key access error deta hai.
in_this_project: `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` mein `cur_key` / `prev_key` construction. `src/lua/token_bucket.lua` sirf `KEYS[1]`. README 'NOT implemented': 'Redis Cluster: NOT tested ... A hash tag in the key (e.g. {user42}) would keep them together -- not done or tested here.' PLAN: Lua project 1 se unchanged reuse ka decision.

Hash tag fix library change ke bina key function se possible
Bring-your-own-client: cluster client plug ho sakta hai
disadvantages: Sliding window undeclared keys use karta hai -- cluster par risk
Hash tag ek hot user ko ek node par pin karta hai (waise bhi hota)
Kuch bhi tested nahi
common_mistakes: Single-node par pass hua toh Cluster par bhi chalega maan lena

Script ko KEYS bina declare kiye keys banane dena

advanced.alternatives: Window keys KEYS mein pass karna (client cur/prev start compute kare -- lekin tab Redis TIME ka fayda chala jaata hai); ya window counters ek HASH ke fields mein (ek key); ya hash tag.

question: How would you choose the numbers for an API limit, a login limit and an OTP limit?
answer_hinglish:
Number guess nahi, limit ka PURPOSE se nikalte hain. Do kisam ki limits hain: capacity limits (server ko bachana) aur security limits (guessing rokna).

API (capacity): legit client ka normal pattern dekho -- page load par kitni requests ek saath (burst) aur steady rate kya. Token bucket isi ke liye hai: README ka example `capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5` -- 20 ka burst, phir 5/s. Burst capacity = ek page / ek sync ka peak; refill = sustained rate jo server per client afford kar sake. Logs se p99 client rate nikalo aur uske upar headroom do. Pehle generous, phir tighten.

Login (security): sliding window, README example `limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000`. Socho: legit user galat password kitni baar karta hai? 3-5. Attacker ko 5 per 15 min = 480 per day per account -- weak password bhi jaldi nahi milega. Per-IP limit thodi dheeli (ek office NAT ke peeche bahut users).

OTP (security): math se. 6-digit OTP = 10^6 combinations. 5 attempts per OTP lifetime ka matlab success probability 5/10^6. Per phone number limit bhi -- SMS bhejne ka paisa lagta hai (SMS pumping). Yeh numbers library mein built-in nahi hain; yeh mera reasoning hai, project mein OTP limit ka koi example config ya test nahi hai.

Teeno mein: `cost` option se mehenge endpoints (bulk = 5) zyada units le sakte hain. Aur yaad rakho cost > limit `RateLimitError` hai.
why_needed: Bahut tight limit = legit users ko 429, support tickets. Bahut dheeli = koi protection nahi. Numbers ka reasoning interview mein senior-ness dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant buffet: 'ek baar mein 3 plate, phir har 10 min ek' (token bucket) vs locker ka PIN: '15 min mein 5 galat try' (security window).
how_it_works: Token bucket: capacity = burst, refillPerSec = steady. Sliding window: limit per windowMs, edges par smooth. Dono `cost` support karte hain; cost limit se zyada ho toh error.
in_this_project: README 'Use it' section: `slidingWindow({ limit: 5, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 })` login ke liye aur `tokenBucket({ capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5 })` API ke liye. PLAN: 'Token bucket ... most API limits' aur 'sliding window counter ... login / OTP style limits'. `src/limiter.ts` cost > limit check.

question: You deploy behind nginx and every user suddenly shares one limit. What happened and how do you roll this out correctly?
answer_hinglish:
Classic: default `trustedProxies: 0` hai, toh limiter socket address use karta hai -- aur nginx ke peeche socket address hamesha NGINX ka hai. Saare users ek key `ip:<nginx ip>` mein, pehle 20 requests ke baad sab ko 429. Yeh secure default ka cost hai: galat config par limit TIGHT hoti hai, bypassable nahi.

Fix aur rollout steps:
1. Topology likho: client -> (CDN?) -> load balancer -> nginx -> app. App ke aage kitne proxies hain jo HAMARE hain?
2. Har proxy X-Forwarded-For APPEND kare (nginx: `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;`). Agar koi proxy header pass hi nahi karta, chain toot jaati hai.
3. `keyByIp({ trustedProxies: n })` -- n = hamare proxies ki ginti. README example: 'behind ONE nginx / load balancer' -> 1.
4. Staging mein verify: ek request bhejo jismein khud ka fake `X-Forwarded-For: 6.6.6.6`; jo key bani woh tumhara asli IP honi chahiye, 6.6.6.6 nahi. Yahi repo ka test hai: `6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.x` with 1 trusted proxy -> clients alag pehchane gaye.
5. App ko sirf proxy se reachable rakho (firewall / private subnet). Agar app port public hai, client seedha connect karke header forge kar sakta hai aur n-th entry uski hogi.

Galti ulti taraf bhi hoti hai: n zyada rakha toh client ka likha entry trust ho jaata hai -- bypass. Mutation H2 (off by one) 5 tests fail karta hai, matlab yeh number sensitive hai. Monitoring: top keys dekho -- agar ek hi IP sab traffic ka owner dikhe, config galat hai. Library mein yeh metric built-in nahi hai.
why_needed: Production rollout ka sabse common rate-limit incident yahi hai. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap symptom se root cause tak jaa sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Society ke gate par guard sirf delivery van ka number note kare, andar ke parcel ka address nahi -- toh saare ghar ek hi 'customer' lagenge.
how_it_works: `clientIp` chain = XFF hops + socket address; index `length - 1 - trustedProxies`. 0 par socket address; n par right se n-th.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts::keyByIp` aur `clientIp`. README: `app.use("/api", rateLimit(apiLimit, { key: keyByIp({ trustedProxies: 1 }) })); // behind ONE nginx / load balancer`. Test `test/express.test.ts` 'behind one trusted proxy'.

Ek number se topology describe
Staging mein forged-header check se verify

Library 'one IP owns all traffic' warning nahi deti

question: How would you monitor that the rate limiter is degraded or failing in production?
answer_hinglish:
Teen signal chahiye: (1) primary store (Redis) fail ho raha hai, (2) decisions fallback se aa rahe hain (degraded), (3) requests bina limit ke jaa rahi hain (fail-open) ya 503 ho rahi hain (fail-closed). Library inmein se kuch hooks deti hai, metrics nahi.

Jo hai:
- `FailoverStore` ka `onError(error)`: primary ki HAR failure par call hota hai -- README example `logger.warn({ err: e }, "rate-limit store failed")`. Isse counter bana do: `ratelimit_store_errors_total`. Throwing onError ignore hota hai (telemetry decision nahi badalti, test hai).
- `Decision.degraded: true`: fallback se aaye decisions par. Lekin dhyaan do: Express / Nest adapters decision ko app ko EXPOSE nahi karte -- na `req` par lagate, na koi callback. Toh middleware use karte ho toh degraded flag tum dekh hi nahi paoge; `onError` count hi proxy hai (har degraded decision ke peeche ek onError hota hai). Direct `limiter.consume()` use karo toh flag milta hai. (README 'When Redis is down' yeh khud likhta hai: degraded adapters se app tak nahi jaata, `onError` hi signal hai.)
- Breaker state: resilience-kit ke policies `onEvent` dete hain (`breaker-state`, `timeout`) -- guard mein unhe pass karo.

Jo NAHI hai: fail-open (`allow`) requests ka koi counter ya log -- woh silently `next()` hoti hain (README: 'requests failed open are not counted anywhere -- add logging around it'). 503 / 429 counts HTTP access logs se nikalne padenge. Built-in metrics, Prometheus exporter -- kuch nahi.

Alerts: store error rate > 0 for 1 min (Redis issue), breaker open, 503 rate on login, aur 429 rate ka sudden change (config bug ya attack).
why_needed: Degraded mode ka khatra yeh hai ki woh CHUPCHAAP kaam karta rehta hai -- N instances par N x limit. Agar koi notice na kare toh 'temporary' fallback hafton chal sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Car ka spare tyre: gaadi chalti rahegi, par dashboard par light jalni chahiye -- warna aap spare par hi 100 km/h highway par chalte rahoge.
how_it_works: FailoverStore catch block: `onError?.(error)` try/catch mein (throw ignore), phir fallback ya StoreUnavailableError. Fallback decision `{ ...decision, degraded: true }`. Adapters decision sirf headers ke liye use karte hain.
in_this_project: `src/failover-store.ts::FailoverStore` (`onError`, `degraded`), `src/types.ts::Decision` (`degraded?: true`). Tests `test/failover.test.ts`: 'primary fails, fallback set' -> 3 calls, `errors` length 3, sab degraded; 'a throwing onError changes nothing'. Mutations F1 (not marked degraded, 3 failures) aur F4 (throwing onError not contained).
advantages: onError har failure par -- simple counter hook
Telemetry failure decision nahi badalti
degraded flag direct API users ke liye
disadvantages: Adapters degraded flag expose nahi karte
Fail-open requests ka koi hook nahi
Built-in metrics nahi
common_mistakes: Sirf Redis ka uptime monitor karna, limiter ka path nahi
onError mein heavy kaam (sync network call) -- har request slow
Har onError par full stack log -- outage mein log flood
follow_up_questions: Fail-open requests ko count karne ke liye adapter mein kya badloge?
Log flood ko kaise rokoge (outage mein har request ek warn)?
Degraded decisions ko response header mein dikhana chahiye kya?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Outage mein onError har request par -- 10k rps par 10k log lines/s. Breaker open hone ke baad bhi har call breaker rejection se fail hota hai -> onError phir bhi chalta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Adapter option `onDecision(decision, req)` callback; ya `req.rateLimit` par decision attach karna (express-rate-limit jaisa); ya OpenTelemetry spans.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale par per-request logging nahi, sampled logs + counters. Per-instance degraded state ko aggregate dashboard mein dekhna.

question: Redis is restarted or fails over during traffic. Walk through what ratelimit-kit does.
answer_hinglish:
Teen alag cheezein ho sakti hain, aur library har ek ko alag handle karti hai.

1. Script cache gaya (NOSCRIPT). Redis restart, `SCRIPT FLUSH`, ya naya primary jisne script kabhi load nahi kiya -- EVALSHA par `NOSCRIPT` aata hai. RedisStore error message mein 'NOSCRIPT' dekh ke `SCRIPT LOAD` karta hai, SHA verify karta hai (mismatch par error), aur EVALSHA ek baar retry. Users ko kuch pata nahi chalta. Test: SCRIPT FLUSH ke baad agla consume `{ allowed: true, remaining: 1 }`. Mutation R1 (NOSCRIPT not handled) 2 tests fail. Design reason (PLAN): EVAL har request par poora script bhejta; EVALSHA ke saath script body sirf restart ke baad ek baar jaata hai.

2. Data gaya. Non-persistent Redis restart par sab keys khaali -> har client fresh limit. Failover mein async replication ki wajah se last kuch writes missing -> thoda dheela. Library isko detect nahi karti -- yeh by design acceptable loss hai.

3. Restart ke DAURAN Redis unreachable. Connection refused / timeout. Yahan FailoverStore kaam aata hai: guard ka timeout (e.g. 50 ms) hanging calls ko kaat-ta hai, breaker baar baar dead Redis ko call karna rokta hai, fallback MemoryStore per-instance limit deta hai (`degraded: true`). Ek subtle side effect (README, code se inferred, tested nahi): timeout ke baad bhi Redis command baad mein chal sakti hai (cancel nahi hoti) jabki fallback jawab de chuka -- toh woh request dono stores mein gini ja sakti hai. FailoverStore nahi hai toh error seedha adapter ke `onStoreError` tak: allow / deny 503 / error.

Failover ke baad ek aur trap: purane primary se juda connection READONLY de sakta hai -- woh retry nahi hota, client ko reconnect karna hoga (library ka kaam nahi, bring-your-own-client).
why_needed: Redis maintenance aur failovers routine hain. Rate limiter ko unke dauran predictable behave karna chahiye -- na hang, na silently unlimited.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ka billing machine restart hua: (1) software dobara load (NOSCRIPT), (2) aaj ki entries udd gayi (data loss), (3) restart ke 2 minute mein haath se parchi (fallback).
how_it_works: `consume`: `load(file)` source + SHA (module-level cache). `evalsha`; catch: NOSCRIPT nahi toh rethrow; warna `scriptLoad(source)`, `loaded !== sha` toh error, phir evalsha. FailoverStore guard ke through primary call karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts::RedisStore` aur `load()`; `src/failover-store.ts::FailoverStore`. Tests: `test/redis.test.ts` (NOSCRIPT after SCRIPT FLUSH; other errors not retried), `test/failover.test.ts` (timeout 100 ms to fallback; breaker: 10 checks, 3 calls). README: 'if Redis answers NOSCRIPT (restart, SCRIPT FLUSH, failover) the script is loaded and the call retried once.'
advantages: NOSCRIPT transparent recovery, sirf ek retry
SHA verification se galat script kabhi nahi chalti
Unreachable phase ke liye clear options (fallback / allow / deny)
disadvantages: Data loss detect nahi hota
NOSCRIPT detection message string par
Restart ke time har instance apni NOSCRIPT recovery khud karta hai (thundering SCRIPT LOAD, chhota cost)
common_mistakes: Har request par EVAL use karna (bandwidth + parse cost)
NOSCRIPT par infinite retry loop
Failover ko sirf 'Redis down' samajhna -- READONLY aur data loss bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: SHA mismatch kab ho sakta hai?
Failover ke baad replication lag ka limit par asar?
Do instances ek saath SCRIPT LOAD karein toh problem?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: EVALSHA + NOSCRIPT retry: bandwidth bachata hai par ek extra round trip restart ke baad. EVAL: simple par har request par script body. Project ne EVALSHA chuna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis flapping: baar baar NOSCRIPT + timeouts; breaker isko smooth karta hai. Failover ke baad stale connection READONLY -- retry nahi, reconnect chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: Redis 7 Functions (`FUNCTION LOAD`) persist hote hain RDB/AOF mein aur replicate hote hain -- NOSCRIPT jaisa problem kam. Yahan use nahi kiya.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada instances = restart ke baad zyada parallel SCRIPT LOAD, par har ek idempotent aur chhota. Scale par koi badi problem nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Redis Functions evaluate karna, failover-aware client config document karna, restart ke baad 'limits reset' event log karna. Abhi implement nahi.

question: Your app runs in two regions. How would you rate-limit across them with this library?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest: multi-region is project mein BUILT nahi hai. PLAN ka 'Not in scope' kehta hai 'Distributed limits without Redis (gossip)', aur README ka saara correctness claim EK Redis par hai (3 instances, exactly 500 of 500; 2 Express instances, exactly 10 of 10).

Options jo main interview mein discuss karunga:

1. Per-region Redis, per-region limit (simplest). Har region apna Redis, `RedisStore` wahi. Ek client jo dono regions hit kare usko 2 x limit milega. Usually acceptable kyunki users ek region par geo-routed hote hain. Login jaise security limit ke liye: limit ko half karo per region, ya user ko home region pin karo.

2. Ek global Redis. Har check cross-region round trip -- tens of ms latency har request par, aur us region ke liye Redis ek single point of failure. Rate-limit check request path par hai, toh yeh usually bura hai.

3. Local + async sync. Har region locally limit kare aur counts periodically exchange kare (CRDT counters / gossip). Approximate, eventual. Yeh library mein nahi hai.

Library mein jo cheez useful hai: `Store` interface (`consume(algorithm, key, cost)`) chhota hai -- ek custom multi-region store likha ja sakta hai bina adapters badle. Aur FailoverStore pattern: region ka Redis down ho toh memory fallback.

Mera recommendation: option 1, per-region limits, security limits ko conservative (split) karke, aur geo-routing sticky. Global exactness ki zaroorat billing quotas ko hoti hai, jo is project ke scope se bahar hai ('quotas over days with billing' not in scope).
why_needed: Multi-region system design interviews ka favourite twist hai. Yahan answer trade-off hai: exactness vs latency vs availability.
real_world_analogy: Do shehron ki branches wala bank: har branch apni daily cash-withdrawal limit track kare (fast), ya har withdrawal par HQ ko phone kare (slow, HQ down = sab band). Usually branch-local + home branch rule.
how_it_works: Per-region: N regions = up to N x limit for a roaming client. Global: latency = cross-region RTT per check. Async sync: limit = local + lag window ka overshoot.
in_this_project: `src/limiter.ts::Store` interface (custom store ka hook), `src/failover-store.ts` (fallback pattern). PLAN 'Not in scope' aur README load test (single Redis). Multi-region ka koi code, config ya test nahi hai.
advantages: Per-region: local latency, region isolation
Store interface se custom strategy possible
FailoverStore har region mein kaam karta hai
disadvantages: Roaming client ko N x limit
Global exactness nahi
Multi-region kuch bhi tested nahi
common_mistakes: Global Redis ko har request path par rakhna
Redis cross-region replication se 'shared' limit maan lena (replica writes refuse karta hai)
Security limits ko per-region full value dena
follow_up_questions: CRDT G-counter rate limiting mein kaise use hoga?
Region failover par user doosre region gaya toh uski limit ka kya?
Billing quota aur rate limit mein design ka fark?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Exact global limit = cross-region coordination = latency + availability risk. Per-region = fast aur available, par N x overshoot. Rate limiting mein overshoot usually sasta hai, latency mehengi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Inter-region link down: global Redis design mein ek region ke saare checks fail. Per-region design mein kuch nahi hota. Region failover mein users naye region par fresh limit paate hain.
advanced.alternatives: Redis Enterprise active-active (CRDT), edge rate limiting (CDN / API gateway), ya token budget allocation: global limit ko regions mein divide karke periodically rebalance.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x regions = 10x overshoot per-region design mein -- tab budget split ya async sync zaroori ho jaata hai.

question: Why can't each app instance just use its own MemoryStore in production?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki har instance sirf apni requests dekhta hai. 3 instances, har ek ka apna MemoryStore, limit 500: load balancer requests baant-ta hai, har instance apne hisaab se 500 tak allow karega -- total up to 3 x 500. Limit utni hi weak ho jaati hai jitne instances.

Yeh project mein MEASURE kiya gaya hai. Load test (`bench/load.mjs`): 3 Express instances alag Node processes mein, ek shared key, sliding window limit 500 per 10 minutes. RedisStore ke saath (run 1): exactly 500 allowed, 503 denied. MemoryStore ke saath: 1116 allowed, 0 denied -- 'N instances, up to N x the limit' warning, measured. (Wahi run; machine Windows 11, Ryzen 5 4500. Run 2 ne shared key par sirf 410 requests bheji, toh limit tak pahuncha hi nahi -- usse cap ke baare mein kuch prove nahi hota. Throughput numbers invalid declared hain, PC 90-100% busy tha.)

Ek aur deterministic test har `npm test` par: do Express instances, ek Redis, 30 concurrent requests -> exactly 10 of 10.

Toh MemoryStore kab? Single instance app, dev, tests, ya Redis ke down hone par FailoverStore ka fallback (decisions `degraded: true`). Aur Redis ke saath correctness isliye hai kyunki poora read-decide-write ek Lua script hai -- atomic, toh concurrent requests last token do baar nahi le sakte (3 clients, 300 requests, capacity 50 -> exactly 50).
why_needed: Horizontal scaling rate limiting ka pehla trap hai: local state distributed system mein shared state nahi hota.
real_world_analogy: Teen counters wala cinema: har counter ka apna 'sirf 100 tickets' register. Teeno 100 bechenge -- hall mein 300 log, seats 100.
how_it_works: MemoryStore = process ke andar ek `Map`. RedisStore = ek shared Redis, Lua script atomic. Dono same `Store` interface aur same algorithm (`step()` vs Lua, parity test se identical).
in_this_project: `src/memory-store.ts` comment: 'With several instances each has its own counts (N instances -> up to N x the limit)'. `bench/load.mjs` (`INSTANCES = 3`, `LIMIT = 500`), results `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-load-run1.json`. `test/express.test.ts` 'two Express instances sharing one Redis'.
advantages: Redis: ek limit sab instances ke liye, measured exact
MemoryStore: zero infra, fast, dev ke liye perfect
Same API, store swap karna ek line
disadvantages: Redis ek extra network hop aur dependency
MemoryStore multi-instance mein misleading -- code chalega, limit kamzor

question: A mobile client team asks how to react to your rate limiter. What do you tell them?
answer_hinglish:
Unhe teen cheezein batata hoon: status codes, headers, aur retry rule.

Status codes:
- 429 = TUM limit cross kar gaye. Body `{"error":"rate_limited",...}`. Ruko aur retry karo.
- 503 with `{"error":"rate_limit_unavailable"}` = HUMARI taraf problem (limiter ka store down, login jaise fail-closed route). Client ki galti nahi; `Retry-After: 5` ke baad retry.
- Normal 500 bhi aa sakta hai agar route default `onStoreError: "error"` par ho.

Headers (har limited response par, jab tak route ne `headers: false` na kiya ho):
- `RateLimit-Limit` -- limit.
- `RateLimit-Remaining` -- kitne units bache. 0 ke paas ho toh client khud slow ho jaaye.
- `RateLimit-Reset` -- seconds (rounded up) jab tak bucket full / window khatam.
- `Retry-After` -- sirf 429 par, seconds, kam se kam 1. Rounded UP, toh is time ke baad retry karna safe hai.

Retry rule: 429 ke baad `Retry-After` jitna ruko, turant retry mat karo (warna wahi 429 aur budget waste -- sliding window denied requests count nahi karta, par loop bandwidth jalata hai). Jitter add karo taaki saare devices ek saath na aayein. Login screen par user ko message dikhao 'X second baad try karo'.

Yeh names IETF 'RateLimit header fields' draft ke hain jo zyada libraries bhejti hain; newer draft ke combined `RateLimit` / `RateLimit-Policy` headers nahi bheje jaate (README: not implemented).
why_needed: API contract sirf success responses ka nahi, throttling ka bhi hota hai. Clients agar Retry-After ignore karein toh retry storms banti hain.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ka token system: display par 'aapka number 15 min mein' (Retry-After). Har minute reception par jaake poochna (retry loop) kuch nahi badalta.
how_it_works: Adapter: decision -> `rateLimitHeaders` -> allowed ho toh `next()`, warna 429 + JSON. Retry-After = `max(1, ceil(retryAfterMs/1000))`, Reset = `ceil(resetMs/1000)`.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts` (header names, bodies, `STORE_UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AFTER_S = 5`), `src/adapters/express.ts`. Tests: `test/express.test.ts` (remaining '2','1','0' phir 429), `test/ip.test.ts` (2001 ms -> '3', 0 ms -> '1'). Mutations H6 (Retry-After may be 0) aur H7 (Reset rounded down) dono pakde gaye.
advantages: Standard headers, client libraries samajhti hain
429 vs 503 se client ko blame clear
Retry-After rounded up -- early retry nahi
disadvantages: Headers seconds mein -- sub-second precision nahi
Newer combined header format nahi
common_mistakes: 429 par turant retry loop

question: Redis is unreachable. What does each onStoreError mode do, and how was it tested with a real client?
answer_hinglish:
Jab store se decision nahi milta (aur FailoverStore ka fallback nahi hai ya woh bhi fail hua), adapter ka `onStoreError` decide karta hai:

- `"error"` (default): error framework ko -- Express `next(err)`, Nest exception layer (500). Route nahi chalta.
- `"allow"` (fail OPEN): request jaati hai, unlimited, BINA RateLimit-* headers. Capacity limits ke liye -- sabko refuse karna thodi der limit na lagane se bura hai.
- `"deny"` (fail CLOSED): 503, `Retry-After: 5`, `{"error":"rate_limit_unavailable"}`. Security limits ke liye.

Testing interesting hai: mock nahi, REAL ioredis client ek closed port (`redis://127.0.0.1:1`) par, real Express app ke peeche. Client options: `enableOfflineQueue: false`, `maxRetriesPerRequest: 0`, `retryStrategy: () => null`, `lazyConnect: true`. Kyun? ioredis default mein disconnected hone par commands QUEUE karta hai aur reconnect ka wait karta hai -- test hang ho jaata. Yeh options command ko turant fail karwate hain. (Production mein ioredis ki yahi default queueing ek hanging request bana sakti hai -- isliye guard ka timeout zaroori hai.)

Results: allow -> `[200, 200, 200]` aur `ratelimit-limit` header null; deny -> `[503, "5", "rate_limit_unavailable"]`; error -> 'error handler'; FailoverStore + MemoryStore fallback -> `[200, 200, 429]` (capacity 2, local limit). Mutation O4 (allow aur deny swapped) 2 tests fail.
why_needed: 'Redis down hai toh kya?' har rate-limiter interview ka sawaal hai. Ek default answer nahi hai -- limit ke purpose par depend karta hai, isliye per-limit choice.
real_world_analogy: Building ka electronic gate bijli jaane par: shopping mall ka gate khula chhod do (fail open, crowd flow), bank vault ka band rakho (fail closed).
how_it_works: Adapter catch: RateLimitError ya 'error' -> rethrow (Express mein outer `.catch(next)`); 'allow' -> `next()` bina headers; 'deny' -> 503 response directly. Nest mein 'deny' `HttpException(..., SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)` throw karta hai.
in_this_project: `test/failover.test.ts` 'Redis unreachable (real ioredis client, closed port)' describe block, `deadRedis()` helper. `src/adapters/http.ts::OnStoreError`. Nest equivalent `test/nestjs.test.ts` (broken store: allow 200, deny 503, default 500).
advantages: Real client se test -- mock ki assumptions nahi
Har mode ka exact HTTP outcome pinned
Per-route choice
disadvantages: Default 'error' 500 deta hai -- users ko generic error
'allow' mode silently unlimited, koi counter nahi
common_mistakes: Sab routes par ek hi mode
ioredis ki offline queue bhool jaana -- 'Redis down' ka matlab error nahi, HANG ho jaata hai
Fail-open path par fake headers bhejna
follow_up_questions: ioredis offline queue production mein band karni chahiye kya?
Default 'error' kyun, 'allow' kyun nahi?
