question: Redis is not down but hanging. What does the guard's timeout really do, and what can it not do?
answer_hinglish:
Hanging Redis (network partition, overloaded server, long-running command) 'down' se bura hai: connection refused turant fail hota hai, par hang mein har request wait karti rehti hai -- event loop free hai par har request ka latency infinity, aur Node mein pending requests memory mein jama hoti hain.

Guard ka timeout yeh solve karta hai: `TimeoutPolicy({ ms: 50 })` (README example) 50 ms ke baad reject karta hai aur FailoverStore fallback se jawab deta hai. Test: ek store jo kabhi resolve nahi hota (`new Promise(() => {})`), `TimeoutPolicy({ ms: 100 })` -- fallback ka decision `degraded: true` aur 2 s se kam mein. Mutation F2 (guard ignored) pakda gaya.

Ab jo woh NAHI kar sakta: Redis call cancel karna. resilience-kit ka TimeoutPolicy operation ko ek AbortSignal deta hai aur timeout par usko abort karta hai -- lekin FailoverStore ka operation `() => this.primary.consume(...)` signal ignore karta hai, kyunki Redis clients AbortSignal leti hi nahi. README: 'a timeout stops WAITING for it.'

Iska practical matlab:
1. Command ioredis ki queue / socket mein pada hai. Redis wapas aaya toh Lua script chal sakta hai -- token ghata dega -- jabki is request ka decision fallback ne already diya. Toh ek request do jagah count ho sakti hai (Redis + memory).
2. Hang ke dauran bahut saare commands pile up -- client side memory.
3. Har request ko pura timeout (50 ms) wait karna padta hai -- isliye breaker saath mein: kuch failures ke baad breaker open, aur calls bina wait ke seedha fallback.
why_needed: Timeouts sabse misunderstood resilience tool hain. Interviewer check karta hai ki aap 'stop waiting' aur 'stop work' ka fark samajhte ho.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein order ke 20 min baad aap uth ke chale gaye (timeout). Kitchen ko pata nahi -- khana phir bhi banega aur bill bhi ban sakta hai.
how_it_works: TimeoutPolicy: `Promise.race([operation(signal), stopped])`, timer par `controller.abort(new TimeoutError(ms))`. FailoverStore catch -> onError -> fallback. Primary ka promise background mein pending rehta hai.
in_this_project: `src/failover-store.ts` comment: 'the Redis call itself cannot be cancelled (clients take no AbortSignal) -- a timeout stops WAITING for it.' `Guard` interface ka `execute(operation: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>, signal?)`. Test `test/failover.test.ts` 'a HANGING primary times out after 100 ms'. resilience-kit ka `projects/18-resilience/src/timeout.ts`. README NOT implemented: 'Cancelling an in-flight Redis call'.
advantages: Hang ek bounded latency ban jaata hai
Breaker ke saath repeated waits bhi band
Fallback se request phir bhi limited
disadvantages: Late Redis execution double-count kar sakta hai
Cancelled nahi hua kaam client queue mein jama
Timeout chhota rakha toh slow-but-healthy Redis par bhi false failovers
common_mistakes: Timeout ko 'cancel' samajhna
Timeout bina breaker -- outage mein har request 50 ms extra
Timeout Redis ke p99 latency se kam rakhna
follow_up_questions: Timeout value kaise choose karoge (50 ms kyun)?
Late execution ka double count kitna bura hai rate limiting mein?
ioredis ka commandTimeout option isse kaise compare karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Library-level timeout (guard) vs client-level (`commandTimeout` jaisa ioredis option): guard client-agnostic hai, par client-level option command ko client queue se bhi nikaal sakta hai. Project ne bring-your-own-client ke wajah se guard chuna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Partition heal hone par queued commands ek saath Redis par -- spike, aur unke tokens 'kharch' ho jaate hain jinke decisions fallback de chuka. Kuch users thodi der zyada strict limit dekhenge.
advanced.alternatives: Client ka `enableOfflineQueue: false` (dead-port test jaisa) + commandTimeout; ya connection-level health check jo breaker ko feed kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: High rps par hang ke dauran pending commands ka backlog tezi se badhta hai -- breaker ka jaldi open hona zyada important ho jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Client-level command timeout documentation, offline queue off recommendation, late-completion metrics. Cancellation NOT implemented (README).

question: While Redis is down the fallback MemoryStore answers. What exactly gets weaker, and what happens when Redis comes back?
answer_hinglish:
Fallback se limit bachi rehti hai, par teen tarah se kamzor:

1. N x limit. Har instance ka apna MemoryStore, toh N instances par client up to N x limit le sakta hai. FailoverStore ka comment yahi kehta hai. Load test ne MemoryStore mode mein yeh measure kiya (3 instances, limit 500 -> 1116 allowed).

2. Cold start. Fallback MemoryStore khaali shuru hota hai (ya purani state ke saath). Jo client Redis mein apni limit khatam kar chuka tha, fallback par uska bucket full hai -- ek fresh allowance.

3. maxKeys eviction. MemoryStore LRU se purani keys drop karta hai (default 100 000) -- drop = reset.

Ab Redis wapas aaya: fallback ke counts Redis mein MERGE NAHI hote (README NOT implemented). Redis wahi state dikhayega jo outage se pehle thi (agar keys expire nahi hui) -- outage ke dauran allowed requests Redis ko pata hi nahi. Matlab recovery ke baad bhi ek window tak limit dheeli. Ulta case bhi: timeout wale late commands Redis mein chale -- woh extra count kar sakte hain.

Recovery kaun detect karta hai? Agar guard mein breaker hai, toh `openMs` (README example 10 s) ke baad breaker trial call bhejta hai; success par Redis phir primary. Bina breaker ke har request Redis try karti hai, toh recovery turant.

Decisions `degraded: true` marked hote hain, toh direct `consume()` callers jaan sakte hain. Fallback khud fail ho toh woh bhi chhupta nahi: `StoreUnavailableError('rate-limit store and fallback unavailable')` (mutation F5).

Security limits par yeh weakness socho: login ke liye fallback ki jagah 'deny' behtar ho sakta hai.
why_needed: Graceful degradation tabhi safe hai jab aapko pata ho ki 'degraded' ka exact matlab kya hai -- kitna dheela aur kitni der tak.
real_world_analogy: Main server down to har branch apna local register use kare. Branch registers baad mein HQ mein enter nahi kiye gaye -- toh HQ ke hisaab se un dino koi transaction hua hi nahi.
how_it_works: Primary fail -> onError -> `fallback.consume(...)` -> `{ ...decision, degraded: true }`. Fallback throw kare -> StoreUnavailableError with cause. Koi reconciliation step nahi.
in_this_project: `src/failover-store.ts::FailoverStore`. Tests `test/failover.test.ts`: 'primary fails, fallback set' -> `[[true,true],[true,true],[false,true]]`; 'the fallback fails too' -> StoreUnavailableError; dead-port Express test fallback ke saath `[200, 200, 429]`. README NOT implemented: 'While degraded, the fallback's counts are per instance and are NOT merged back into Redis when it returns.'
advantages: Outage mein bhi koi na koi limit
Degraded decisions marked
Fallback failure loud, hidden nahi
disadvantages: N x limit, cold start, eviction resets
No merge-back after recovery
Security limits ke liye shayad bahut dheela
common_mistakes: Fallback ko 'same limit' samajhna
Login par fallback lagake fail-closed expect karna
Fallback ko bhi Redis bana dena (same failure domain)
follow_up_questions: Fallback limit ko limit / N set karoge toh kya problem?
Merge-back kaise design karoge?
Breaker ka half-open recovery yahan kaise kaam karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Availability (kuch limit) vs correctness (exact limit). Fallback availability chunta hai. Alternative 'deny' correctness/security chunta hai. Per-limit decision.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Long outage: hours tak N x limit. Instance restart during outage: memory state gaya, phir fresh. Autoscaling during outage: N badha, limit aur dheela.
advanced.alternatives: Fallback limit ko conservatively scale (limit / expected N) -- ek wrapper Algorithm se; ya secondary Redis; ya fail-closed for security limits.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x instances = 10x overshoot during outage. Bade fleet par fallback ka 'still a limit' claim kamzor ho jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Scaled fallback limits, outage ke baad reconciliation (fallback counts ko Redis mein INCRBY), degraded duration alerts. Sab NOT implemented.

question: Why is failover a Store wrapper with a structural Guard interface, instead of logic inside the adapters or a dependency on resilience-kit?
answer_hinglish:
Do design decisions hain, PLAN mein dono likhe hain.

1. Store wrapper (decorator pattern). `FailoverStore` khud ek `Store` hai: `new FailoverStore(primary, { guard, fallback, onError })`. RateLimiter ko pata hi nahi ki uske neeche failover hai. Fayda: 'Redis ke badle kya' EK jagah hai -- Express, Nest, ya direct `consume()` caller, sab ko same behaviour. Agar yeh adapters mein hota toh har framework adapter mein duplicate hota aur direct API users ko milta hi nahi. Adapters ke paas sirf ek sawaal bacha: jab KUCH bhi nahi bacha, request ka kya (`onStoreError`). Clean split: store = 'what instead', adapter = 'what if nothing'.

2. Structural Guard. `interface Guard { execute<T>(operation: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> }` -- exactly resilience-kit ke `Policy` ka shape. TypeScript structural typing hai, toh `wrap(new CircuitBreaker(...), new TimeoutPolicy(...))` bina import ke fit ho jaata hai. ratelimit-kit ki zero runtime dependencies rehti hain; koi bhi apna guard (ek simple timeout wrapper, cockatiel jaisi library ka adapter) de sakta hai. Test bhi yahi respect karta hai: resilience-kit ko dynamic import se load karta hai (`../../18-resilience/src/index.js`) 'so this package keeps no compile-time dependency on it'.

Cost: guard ka signal FailoverStore use nahi karta (Redis clients signal nahi lete), aur structural typing ka matlab hai ki resilience-kit ka shape badla toh compile time par kuch nahi tootega -- sirf runtime / tests.
why_needed: Library design mein yeh dikhata hai ki aap responsibilities kahan baant-te ho aur coupling kaise avoid karte ho -- senior interviews ka core.
real_world_analogy: Bijli ka inverter ghar ke main switchboard par lagta hai, har appliance ke andar nahi. Aur inverter koi bhi brand ka ho, plug ka shape standard hai.
how_it_works: FailoverStore.consume: guard ? guard.execute(run) : run(); catch -> onError (contained) -> fallback (degraded) / StoreUnavailableError. Adapters StoreUnavailableError ko baaki non-RateLimitError errors jaisa treat karte hain.
in_this_project: `src/failover-store.ts` (`Guard`, `FailoverStoreOptions`, `FailoverStore`), `src/limiter.ts::Store`, `projects/18-resilience/src/types.ts` (Policy shape). PLAN: 'failover is a Store wrapper, not adapter logic' aur 'the guard is structural (execute(op, signal)), so resilience-kit's breaker and timeout plug in with no dependency between the packages'.

Zero runtime dependency
Composable: koi bhi Store primary/fallback ho sakta hai
disadvantages: Structural coupling compile-time par invisible
Signal unused -- interface promise zyada karta hai jitna use hota hai
Adapter aur store dono error handling mein -- do jagah padhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Failover ko har adapter mein copy karna
resilience-kit ko hard dependency banana sirf ek interface ke liye
FailoverStore ko FailoverStore mein nest karna bina soche (double degraded)
follow_up_questions: Decorator pattern ke aur examples is codebase mein?
Guard interface mein signal kyun hai agar use nahi hota?
Structural vs nominal typing ka risk kaise test se cover kiya?

advanced.alternatives: Adapter option `fallbackStore`; ya RedisStore ke andar built-in timeout; ya resilience-kit ko peer dependency.

question: How do the circuit breaker and the timeout work together as the guard, and what did the breaker test prove?
answer_hinglish:
Guard = `wrap(new CircuitBreaker({ openMs: 10_000 }), new TimeoutPolicy({ ms: 50 }))` (README example). `wrap(a, b)` ka matlab `a(b(call))` -- breaker BAHAR, timeout ANDAR. Order kyun? Timeout har Redis call ko bound karta hai; uska TimeoutError breaker ko ek failure ki tarah dikhta hai. Toh hanging Redis bhi breaker ko open kar sakta hai -- sirf connection-refused nahi.

Breaker kya deta hai jo timeout nahi deta? Timeout ke saath bhi har request 50 ms wait karti (ya refused hone ka round trip). Breaker kuch failures ke baad OPEN ho jaata hai, aur phir calls ko Redis tak bhejta hi nahi -- turant reject, FailoverStore turant fallback. `openMs` ke baad half-open trial; success par close. (Breaker internals resilience-kit ke hain, yeh project sirf use karta hai.)

Test: breaker `windowSize: 3, minimumCalls: 3, openMs: 60_000` + timeout 100 ms, ek dead store jo hamesha throw kare, 10 checks (`k0`..`k9`). Dead store ko calls: exactly 3. Pehle 3 failures ne breaker khola, baaki 7 seedha fallback gaye. Mutation F2 (guard ignored) yahi aur timeout test todta hai.

Ek nuance: har breaker rejection bhi FailoverStore ke liye 'error' hai -- toh `onError` har request par chalta rahega, breaker open ho tab bhi. Logging ko rate-limit karna padega.

Aur breaker ka state per FailoverStore instance hai: process mein ek instance share karo. Har request par naya guard banaya toh breaker kabhi kuch yaad nahi rakhega.
why_needed: Timeout aur breaker alag problems solve karte hain: timeout ek call ko bound karta hai, breaker repeated calls ko rokta hai. Interview mein dono ka role alag batana zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Phone call: timeout = 30 sec ring ke baad kaat do. Breaker = 3 baar koi nahi uthaya toh agle 10 min call hi mat karo, seedha SMS bhejo (fallback).
how_it_works: wrap composition outermost first. Breaker failure window count karta hai; minimumCalls ke baad threshold cross -> open. Open state mein execute turant reject. FailoverStore rejection ko catch karke fallback.
in_this_project: `test/failover.test.ts` 'guarded by resilience-kit's circuit breaker: once open, the dead primary is not even called' -> `calls.n` 3. resilience-kit: `projects/18-resilience/src/breaker.ts`, `projects/18-resilience/src/wrap.ts`. README: 'a test with a dead store and a breaker of 3 calls made 10 checks and called the dead store only 3 times.'

onError breaker-open par bhi har request

Har request par naya guard instance

question: Walk through the layers of ratelimit-kit and who decides what when Redis fails.
answer_hinglish:
Chaar layers, har ek ka ek kaam:

1. Algorithm (`tokenBucket`, `slidingWindow`): numbers + logic, do roop mein -- TypeScript `step()` aur Lua script. Parity test (600 random steps each, real Redis) prove karta hai ki identical decisions. Yeh 'kitna allow' decide karta hai.

2. Store (`MemoryStore`, `RedisStore`, `FailoverStore`): state kahan aur kaise atomic. RedisStore poora read-decide-write ek Lua script mein (EVALSHA, NOSCRIPT retry, Redis TIME). FailoverStore ek wrapper: primary ko guard (breaker + timeout) ke through call, fail par fallback (`degraded: true`) ya `StoreUnavailableError`. Yeh 'Redis ke BADLE kya' decide karta hai.

3. RateLimiter: ek limit = algorithm + store + prefix. Store chhoone se pehle validation -- key 1-512 chars, cost integer >= 1, cost <= limit -- warna `RateLimitError` (bug). Yeh 'input valid hai kya' decide karta hai.

4. Adapters (Express `rateLimit`, Nest `@RateLimit`): 'client kaun hai' (`keyByIp`, trustedProxies, /64) aur 'HTTP par kya bhejein' (headers, 429). Plus `onStoreError`: jab store layer ke paas koi answer nahi -- error / allow / deny(503). Bug kabhi fail open nahi.

Redis fail scenario end to end: request -> adapter key nikaalta hai -> RateLimiter validate -> FailoverStore -> guard timeout/breaker fails -> onError log -> fallback MemoryStore answers (degraded) -> adapter 200/429. Fallback nahi -> StoreUnavailableError -> adapter: login route 'deny' -> 503 + Retry-After 5; API route 'allow' -> next().

Har layer apna test set: algorithms, limiter, redis, ip, express, nestjs, failover -- 91 tests, 51 mutation checks (49 caught, 2 equivalent).
why_needed: Senior interview mein 'architecture batao' ka matlab hai: boundaries aur responsibilities. Failure path par kaun kya decide karta hai, yeh clear hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Hospital: doctor (algorithm) dose decide karta hai, pharmacy (store) dawa rakhti hai, backup pharmacy (fallback) jab main band ho, reception (adapter) patient pehchaanti hai aur batati hai 'kal aana' (429) ya 'system down hai' (503).
how_it_works: Dependency direction: adapters -> RateLimiter -> Store -> Algorithm. Koi layer upar wali ko nahi jaanti. Errors upar bubble: RateLimitError (bug) aur store errors; adapter class se fark karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/algorithms.ts`, `src/lua/*.lua`, `src/memory-store.ts`, `src/redis-store.ts`, `src/failover-store.ts`, `src/limiter.ts`, `src/adapters/http.ts`, `src/adapters/express.ts`, `src/adapters/nestjs.ts`. Entry points `package.json` exports: `.`, `./express`, `./nestjs` -- Nest optional peer dependency. Stage table PLAN.md mein.

Failure decisions do clear jagah (store: instead, adapter: nothing)

Har route ke liye naya store/guard instance
